issues.legal_issue: A court may require a party to deposit a passport to secure that party’s presence in contempt proceedings.
material_facts: During contempt proceedings arising from an alleged breach of an injunction, the party and a family member repeatedly undertook to clear a charge over property but did not fulfil those undertakings.
The party later failed to appear when directed, had moved abroad without disclosing that address to the court, and the court was concerned that he might leave the country.
The court ordered the party to deposit his passport to secure his presence and the progress of the proceedings; it did not order the passport to be impounded.
issues.conclusion: The direction to deposit the passport was within the court’s jurisdiction and was properly made to secure the party’s presence and the further progress of the trial.
issues.legal_principle: In contempt proceedings, a court may make appropriate orders, including directing the surrender or deposit of a passport, to secure a party’s presence. The Court relied on David Jude v. Hannah Grace Jude, (2003) 10 SCC 767, where directions concerning a contemnor’s passport were made to secure her presence before the court. The underlying application had been brought under Order XXXIX Rule 2A of the Code of Civil Procedure and Sections 10 and 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971.

rule.if: contempt_proceeding and repeated_court_undertakings and undertakings_unfulfilled and (failure_to_appear or undisclosed_foreign_residence or risk_of_leaving_country) and passport_deposit_to_secure_presence

predicates.contempt_proceeding: The proceeding was a contempt proceeding concerning alleged disobedience of a court order.
predicates.repeated_court_undertakings: A party repeatedly gave undertakings to the court.
predicates.undertakings_unfulfilled: The party did not fulfil the undertakings given to the court.
predicates.failure_to_appear: The party failed to appear before the court when directed to do so.
predicates.undisclosed_foreign_residence: The party had moved abroad but did not disclose that residence to the court.
predicates.risk_of_leaving_country: The court had reason to be concerned that the party might leave the country.
predicates.passport_deposit_to_secure_presence: The court directed the party to deposit the passport for the purpose of securing the party’s presence.

issues.definition: When a party in contempt proceedings repeatedly fails to fulfil court undertakings and there is a concern about securing that party’s presence, a passport-deposit order made for that purpose is within the court’s jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A related contempt petition need not be restored when the underlying civil suit has been pending for a long time, its trial has begun, and substantial court time has already been spent on interim and contempt proceedings.
material_facts: The underlying civil suit had been pending for many years and had reached the stage of cross-examination of defence witnesses.
Substantial court time had been spent on interim orders and the contempt petition.
The contempt petition had been disposed of after the appellate court set aside the passport-deposit direction.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to restore the contempt petition and instead directed the civil suit to proceed and be disposed of expeditiously.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the age and procedural stage of the civil suit and the substantial court time already spent on interim orders and contempt proceedings. It cited no earlier case or statutory provision for declining restoration.

predicates.civil_suit_pending: A civil suit underlying the contempt proceedings remained pending.
predicates.trial_commenced: The trial in the civil suit had begun.
predicates.substantial_time_spent_on_interim_and_co: The court had spent substantial time dealing with interim orders and contempt proceedings.
predicates.restoration_of_related_contempt_petition: A party asked the court to restore a related contempt petition that had been disposed of.

issues.definition: Where a civil suit remains pending after trial has begun and substantial court time has already been spent on interim and contempt proceedings, a related contempt petition sought to be restored need not be restored.
